dct_description_sm:
This Feature layer showcases control survey monuments across the province of Newfoundland and Labrador. Control survey Monuments are utilized in legal land surveys, featuring NAD83 CSRS values and the condition of the monuments. 

The three types of survey monuments include:

  • Conventional
  • GPS
  • High Precision GPS.

A geodetic control network is a system of precisely measured points, often arranged in triangular formations, used for control surveying. These networks provide a foundational framework for mapping, charting, and various scientific studies. They are essential for accurate positioning and boundary delineation, supporting applications such as navigation, construction, and resource management. By maintaining the accuracy and consistency of spatial data across different regions and over time, geodetic control networks enable scientific studies in fields like earth sciences, environmental monitoring, and urban planning.

This layer is administered by the GIS and Mapping Division, Department of Forestry, Agriculture and Lands. Information referenced within this dataset represents the most current information available.
